handoff.purpose: Implements _relation_adjacencies (converts forest edges/hyperedges to normalised adjacency dicts) and begins diffuse_relation_scores (initialises frontier and starts loop).

symbols.name: _relation_adjacencies
symbols.note: Private function; converts forest edges and hyperedges into a dict of relation -> (normalised adjacency, direction, source_kind).

symbols.name: diffuse_relation_scores
symbols.note: Public function; diffuses scores along each relation independently. Validates steps and decay, initialises frontier, loops over relations.

claims.text: step, then "two functions that mention the same type" are two hops apart and 1,276,024 of the 2,379,471 possible function pairs become adjacent -- 53.6% of the complete graph, of which ``str`` alone contributes 939,135. A channel that connects half the repository to itself does not rank anything; it normalises everything to the same score and the packer then falls back to node id order. So the type layers ship as a LENS: published for consumers that ask for them by name, never mixed into the score that decides what is read. Turning them into a channel is a separate, gated lane whose precondition is the hub cap in ``index["types"]["coverage"]``.
claims.why: The numbers and behavior described (type layers, hub cap, packer) refer to code and data structures outside this chunk; no evidence in the given code.

claims.text: Filtering by node KIND rather than by relation NAME is deliberate: a name list would have to be edited every time a relation is added, and the edit that is forgotten is the one that reopens this.
claims.why: The filtering logic is not shown in this chunk; only file_ids set is built but not used for filtering by kind in this chunk (used later). The claim is about design rationale, not directly testable here.

claims.text: Directed edges propagate only source-to-target. Hyperedges use explicit member-to-group-to-member message passing, represented here by an equivalent normalised transition for computation; the Forest itself is never rewritten as a clique.
claims.why: The actual propagation logic is not in this chunk; only the loop start is shown. The claim about hyperedge representation and forest rewriting cannot be verified.

claims.text: diffusion decay must be at most 1

observations.what: The docstring of _relation_adjacencies contains a long commentary about type layers and a hub cap that refers to external structures.
The function _relation_adjacencies builds file_ids set but does not use it for filtering in this chunk; it is used in the edge/hyperedge loops to skip non-file nodes.
The variable 'direction' is set to None when conflicting directedness is found; this may be intended to mark mixed-direction relations.
In diffuse_relation_scores, the frontier is initialised from source_scores but the actual diffusion loop (for hop in range(1, steps+1)) is incomplete in this chunk.

The docstring of diffuse_relation_scores claims hyperedges are represented as equivalent normalised transition, but the code in this chunk does not show that representation (only the adjacency built by _relation_adjacencies is used).
